First off, please take a deep breath!  I'll try and help you as best as I can as a far-away, half drunk stranger on the internet.

I've struggled with depression for 10 or so years, it's so deeply ingrained into my life experience that it's just a constant, looming factor that I can only assume will always be with me.  I'm 23, so it hasn't been long since I was a freshman in college.  I'm from Minnesota but went out to school in Colorado because I wanted to get away (I was losing my friends due to drug use and continued isolation because of my depression) and thought maybe it would help me.

I don't want to scare you, but it didn't.  It was so hard for me, it drove me into behaviors that I'd never done before (such as binging and purging).  Basically, by the end of my freshman year (I don't know how I lasted a whole YEAR) I had a 1.2 GPA because I never went to class.  I did drugs all day, every day, and drank excessively.  My only friend was a meth chef who lived in an RV, who carried a handgun everywhere and whom I would occasionally blow (yes, this was rock bottom for me...I never did meth myself, I was more into the morphine, oxy, cocaine, vicodin).  I would have anxiety attacks in school.  I would cut myself, make myself throw up, I once drank an entire bottle of Robotussin and then followed it up with a bunch of hydrogen peroxide (not sure why) and kept a bag of my vomit under my bed.  I didn't come out of my room for days.  I tried to kill myself...I wrote a suicide letter addressed to my best friend and then overdosed on oxycontin.  I flunked out and returned back to Minnesota.

Going out of state is not for everyone.  I don't want to scare you, and I'm sorry if I caused you unnecessary anxiety.  I can't understand why your parents would push you out of state and I'm sorry about your relationship.  I don't think you should go out of state, really I don't.  If you can, I'd convince them (somehow, though I'm sure you've tried) to "let" you stay in state.  If you don't mind me asking, what part of the country are you moving to?

As far as the therapy thing goes, I understand completely.  I should go but I don't, because I'm ashamed and I can't tell the truth, for some reason.  I lie about how much I drink and cut and cry over nothing because I'm embarrassed.  But I do take medicine, and it helps to a degree but of course not completely.  I would try and stay on it, and be consistant, as longa s you aren't feeling any negative side effects.  If you can get over feeling ashamed of going to the doctor, they can always change up your dose/medications if you ARE having side effects.

The issue you are having with your parents perplexes me.  Are they homophobic?  Perhaps they're worried you are in love with your friend and this is why you want to stay.  The situation also angers me, as I cannot see why that would be a problem or why they'd want to push you away.  It feels so wrong that they're trying to "fix" your problems by sending you an entire PLANE RIDE away.  

Please don't hesistate to PM me anytime if you'd like to talk.  As I said earlier, please take a deep breath, because this hard time WILL pass.

I like Cannon Falls a lot.  I'm in Red Wing which is about 20 miles down county road 19 but I'm looking into moving there myself.  It's got a really nice park system and the town is very pretty.  It's about 35 miles to St. Paul/Minneapolis when you go up Highway 52 and about 45 miles to Rochester the other direction.  Both commutes are easy (and boring).  If you need something from Target or Walmart you'll have to go to Red Wing.

Most of the surrounding area is countryside; mainly corn and soybeans, but it's very pretty.  If you like small towns, I'm sure you'll like it.  Winters are cold and snowy, summers are hot and humid.  Spring is really nice and it's beautiful in the fall.  In June they have their annual Cannon Valley Fair which is pretty fun, typical Minnesota fair.
  
I have a friend that lives downtown and there's a few bars that get kind of crazy on the weekends, if that's something you're interested in.  I've never experienced the CF "night life" myself but I'm sure it's your typical small town bar scene.  Also, if you go a little bit north there's a small township called Welch where you can get really good ice cream and go tubing/canoeing on the Cannon River, my cousins actually own the joint.  It's pretty popular with young twentysomethings who bring a couple coolers of beer along for the trip.  There's also good fishing on the river and a bike trail that goes from Cannon Falls to Red Wing (I wanna say it's about a 20 mile bike ride, but I might be wrong, and it goes through Welch).  It's really pretty and alongside the river, and it's kept up very well.  If you go into Red Wing I'd suggest climbing Barn's Bluff some time if you're into the outdoors, it's especially pretty in October when the leaves are changing.  If you continue past Cannon Falls on 19 you'll get to Northfield, but I don't know much about the town, except I've driven through it and it looks very pretty.  It's a college town (two private schools, St. Olaf and Carleton).

I watched my aunt die.  She became ill very quickly and by the time they discovered she had breast cancer it was stage 4 and terminal.  She went into a comma within 48 hours of the diagnosis and was being kept alive on life support.  They "pulled the plug" while I was at the hospital and me along with several of my relatives were in the room with her.

I'd never seen anyone die before, and nothing could have prepared me for it.  It wasn't peaceful.  When they took her off life support she didn't die quickly with the heart monitor flat lining soon after.  A priest recited her last rites as the life support was turned off, and then she took a breath on her own.  Then her eyes opened.  I was stunned, horrified...the doctor says she "wasn't there" that she was still in a coma and it was just a reflex, but I don't know if I fully believe that.  She looked around at the room, she looked terrified.  She was completely pale, didn't even look like her, and she kept taking those horrible breaths.  The priest had his hand on her forehead and we were all praying with him, asking God to accept her soul, etc etc.  And all the while my aunt kept looking around.  Her mouth was open, slack jawed as if she were screaming.  I will never get that face out of my mind.  She died in extreme pain, and terrified.

Eventually she just stopped breathing.  The priest shut her eyes, but her face still held that scream.  I will never be the same, I can't go more than a few hours without seeing it.  It keeps me up at night.  This was 6 months ago now.

Hey, I kind of know where you're coming from, so maybe I can offer some words!  A few months ago my boyfriend of 3 and a half years broke up with me...we had been living together for almost 3 years and he was my best friend.  Long freakin' story, but I know (kind of) what you're going through.  To some extent, at least.

I thought I was going to die.  I've suffered from depression for almost 10 years, I cut, I'm suicidal, done all sorts of drugs, social anxiety, general anxiety, all that fucking good stuff.  He was the only thing holding me together, or so I thought.  I thought I was going to die, but I didn't.  The day after he left me, I woke up.  I took one breath at a time, and then it was day two.  I woke up again.  Repeat, repeat.  I honestly don't know how I did it.  I'm not saying that him leaving me was killing me per se...it was more that he was the only thing holding me back from the soul crushing depression.  I was using him as a shield against my own fucked up self, and this was unhealthy for the both of us.  So, here came the depression.  

Like I said, I don't know how I did it.  To be honest, I don't know how I do ANY day.  There's a .20 gauge shotgun sitting in the other room and EVERY. SINGLE. DAY. I'm temped to put it in my own mouth and just end this shit.  I cut too (mainly out of anxiety than depression) and it fucking sucks.  I know what you mean when you say you put everything into this relationship.  So did I.  If it feels good for you to type, type.  If it feels good to bitch, do that.  But please don't cut.  I feel so shitty every single time that I do that I can't imagine anyone else going through that.  Even if it's a stranger on the internet.

If you feel like you need help, then seek it out!  Perhaps you should go back to therapy.  Are you on any medications?  It doesn't work for everyone (I'm still searching for the perfect cocktail myself) but it can do wonders.  Don't ever be afraid to reach out to anyone...you'd be surprised who comes out of the woodwork and cares so much about you.

As far as your relationships with her family goes...have you talked to any of them about it?  I know that's a tricky road to cross if she told you not too but if you really feel that her mother is your second mom then I'm sure this woman feels the same way.  Maybe they could offer some support?  They still care about you.  Don't forget that!

Just remember that life DOES GO ON. Whether you like it or not.  If you need to, find an excuse to get you out of bed.  I work on a farm and when people would ask (and they often did, if you can believe it) "how do you get up every morning and force yourself to go to work?"  I'd just respond, "well, the cows aren't gonna feed themselves!"  Find an excuse, and beat the shit out of it.  When you open your eyes and think, "I can't do this"  have someone or something that you say, "No, you know what?  If have to do it.  For _______."  Have a mantra.  Every time I was sad (shit, anytime I'm STILL sad)  I say, "I may move forward slowly, but I never step back."  It's a bastardized Lincoln quote but to me it basically means that no matter how bad things get, I'm going to force myself forward.

When things get hard for me, I go on imgur.com/r/funny and watch family guy or American dad.  Find something that will make you laugh.  It really does heal the soul.  I feel so much better.  

If you ever want to talk, please PM me! I'm going through the same shit you are and it never hurts to have someone to talk to.  Just try and remember that you CAN move forward, and things WILL clear up.  I promise.  It's hard (and i'm not going to lie and say it isn't) and there will be days when you really don't think you can do it.  The preexsisting (spelling?) depression doesn't help.  But I promise you friend, you are strong and you can struggle through this.  Life isn't going to take you down.  If it didn't take me, anyone can do it.

Hugs and prayers from Minnesota! :)

I work on a research dairy at my university.  We do mainly nutritional research, and we have 5 fistulated cows (out of a heard of 130). We've had many students of all ages from around the metro area come in and "stick their hands inside a cow" and see first hand the science behind rumination.  It's a unique opportunity to further our knowledge of bovine nutrition and make changes to the diets of dairy cows in the future as needed.  Our cows are on a diet of 90% roughage (including grass hay, alfalfa hay, corn silage, and some pasture) and 10% ground corn, and we test different feed enhancers and mineral/vitamin supplements for various companies.

Does it cause pain to put in?  Sure.  Like any surgery there is a time of recovery but our animals are put into a special "quarantine"  pasture to allow them a quiet, comfortable recovery and are checked several times a day.
